sentences.text: Xericeps was a medium-sized pterosaur known only from a single jaw fragment measuring 173 millimeters in length.
This holotype, representing an adult animal, consists solely of fragmented jaws that lack teeth.
Its wingspan likely fell near the lower end of the 3 to 8 meter range typical for medium-sized pterosaurs.
The upturned jaw features a curved occluding surface when viewed from the side and bears five pairs of elongated holes along its lower edges.
A pair of ridges on the dorsal surface of the jaw symphysis resembles features found in Alanqa and Argentinadraco, yet the shape of these ridges on Xericeps differs from those of Alanqa.
The name Xericeps combines the Greek word for 'dry' referencing the Sahara Desert and the Latin suffix for 'head', alluding to its forceps-like beak.
British paleontologist David M. Martill purchased the holotype specimen directly at the mine site in January 2017.
Xericeps is known solely from this holotype specimen, which was originally described in 2017.
A 2021 study classified Xericeps as a chaoyangopterid closely related to Argentinadraco, and subsequent analyses consistently place Xericeps within the family Alanqidae.
Some sources classify Xericeps within the family Azhdarchidae instead.
Martill and colleagues classified Xericeps within the clade Neoazhdarchia based on the presence of foramina in the jaw, and the Paleobi Database lists the parent group of Xericeps as Neoazhdarchia.
Xericeps lived during the Cenomanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, a time range recorded as the Cenomanian, from 100.5 to 93.9 million years ago.
However, researchers believe Xericeps lived between 93.9 and 113.0 million years ago during the Albian to Cenomanian ages.
The animal inhabited a subtropical alluvial plain characterized by rivers, deltas, and swampy lakes.
This habitat was shared with large theropod dinosaurs like Spinosaurus and Carcharodontosaurus, as well as the sauropod Rebbachisaurus.
The exact diet of Xericeps remains uncertain, though relatives like Alanqa appear to have specialized in hunting hard-shelled mollusks.
